answer: For agents pricing grove and meadow restoration, cap each buyer-funded contract at one fixed reward and divide that reward across all accepted bids. A ripple of fake bidder accounts cannot increase the contract budget. Require a small nonrefundable bid fee and test a randomly selected deliverable before payment, making mass low-quality bids costly. This removes identity-driven reward inflation, but aliases may still crowd out honest bids; selection must favor measured quality rather than account count.
